title: Bridge Lane daily docket
content:
Quick morning brain-dump for Bridge Lane shift. Mostly a working list + short diagnostics I don’t want to lose.

Context / goals:
- Keep the p1 latency pool healthy during expected midday spike (customer A running batch evals).
- Avoid mass preempts during warmup window (we saw 12% tail latency bump last week when scale-out overlapped with cold cache).
- Coordinate small network config change with infra on-call before applying — need to avoid ASG churn.

Morning checkpoints (first 30m)
- Check pool health dashboard (console -> Dedicated -> bridge-lane-pool): look for tokenized request spikes and token throughput per-VM.
- Nodes with high reclaim counters: run `kubectl get nodes -o wide | grep -E \"NotReady|SchedulingDisabled\"`
- Confirm KV cache hit rate: query cache-metrics (prom): `sum(rate(kv_cache_hits[5m])) / sum(rate(kv_cache_lookups[5m]))` -> want >= 0.72

Top of list (urgent)
[ ] 1) Patch INFRA-2019 (driver p0.4): roll to one rack canary (3 nodes) and watch p99 for 10m. If safe, extend to all racks in pool.
 - Steps: tag canary via `label=node-role=canary`, update deployment config `bridge-pool-deploy:v3 -> v3.1-canary`.
 - Rollback command: `kubectl rollout undo deployment/bridge-runtime`

[ ] 2) Prewarm plan for customer-A batch windows (13:00–15:00 PST)
 - Pre-warm schedule: add 5 warm nodes at 12:30; set min-replicas to 18 for 12:30–15:30; scale-down at 15:45.
 - Cost check quick calc: 5 G4dn nodes * 0.48/hr * 3.25 hr = ~7.8 node-hours -> tag as billable to cust-A usage.

[ ] 3) Network baseline test on rack-7 (observed packet drops Mar 11)
 - Run `iperf3 -c ip-10-7-2-11 -t 30` from control host. Capture jitter > 2ms and loss > 0.2% -> escalate to infra net team.
 - Post results to Slack thread and link to INC-4532.

Midday micro-tasks (15m items)
- Sweep failed pods older than 1h in bridge namespace: `kubectl get pods -n bridge --field-selector=status.phase=Failed` -> delete + note recurring labels.
- Check autoscaler logs for scale events between 11:30–12:30; we want to avoid reactive scale loops.
- Look at colocated multi-tenant VMs for noisy neighbors (htop, nvidia-smi sampling).

Diagnostics snippets to keep (for copy/paste)
- Cache warm status: `curl -s http://bridge-metrics.local/kv_status | jq .warm_fraction`
- Current replica count: `kubectl get hpa -n bridge -o jsonpath='{.items[*].status.currentReplicas}'`
- Node reclaim counter: `kubectl get nodes -L reclaim-counter`

Open questions / follow-ups
- Why did we see the 12% p99 bump on Mar 5? hypothesis: overlapping autoscale + cold kv loads. Action: instrument a flag to track whether requests hit cold-kv for first token. (quick eval: instrument trace field `kv_hit_bool` for 2 days on canary only).
- Talk to Maya about evening runbook for preemptive warmdrain vs draining with graceful cache handoff.

Notes for handoff (if I need to leave shift)
- Status: canary patch INFRA-2019 applied to 3 nodes at 12:10 — monitor p99 and backoffs.
- If p99 > baseline + 40ms for 3 consecutive minutes -> rollback and @diego for network check.
- Leave link to this doc in Slack handoff message and tag Diego/Maya.

Random brain sparks (ideas to capture)
- Small experiment: staggered prewarm for different seq lengths (short requests warm smaller LRU sets quicker). Could reduce cost by ~6% on mixed workloads.
- Add small flag on the client to advertise expected sequence length (opt-in) so router can pick quantized model variant.

End-of-shift checklist
[ ] post final metrics (p50/p95/p99, cache-hit, node-count) to the shift channel
[ ] close or update INFRA-2019 with observations
[ ] create follow-up ticket for kv cold-hit tracing (if not done)

— Asha
